source_admission: Primary reports and research checked at the indicated access depth. This is a bounded engineering screen, not a systematic review or full-source scholarly admission.

sources.title: Dickinson and Brown, Radiated microwave power transmission system efficiency measurements (1975)
sources.evidence: 495.62 W received across 1.702 m; 54.18% end-to-end; measured transmitter 68.87% and receiver 78.67%. Does not demonstrate a MW orbital system.

sources.title: Construction and testing of a space ready rectenna (1993)
sources.evidence: Space-oriented rectenna research; approximately 90% RF-to-DC capability described. The study's 85% receiver assumption is an engineering scenario.

sources.title: DARPA POWER demonstration (2025)
sources.evidence: More than 800 W at 8.6 km for 30 s. More than 20% optical-output-to-receiver-electric efficiency measured at shorter distances; neither a wall-plug efficiency nor the 8.6 km efficiency.

sources.title: Ruperto Hernandez et al., Orbital Power-Beaming (2025)
sources.access: NASA abstract and linked conference paper
sources.evidence: 1064 nm fiber-laser concept, coupled orbit/power sizing and electric propulsion. Wavelength motivates the comparison; its concept is not a flight demonstration.

sources.title: Kurs et al., Wireless Power Transfer via Strongly Coupled Magnetic Resonances (2007)
sources.evidence: 60 W at about 40% efficiency over more than 2 m. Kilometre circuits require separate coupling, voltage, reactive power and loss estimates.

sources.title: Ahsun, Dynamics and control of electromagnetic satellite formations (2007)
sources.evidence: Superconducting mutual-force formation control; nonlinear coupling and external-field angular momentum management. Does not establish the tile-scale hardware.

sources.title: Experimental Demonstration of a Decentralized Electromagnetic Formation Flying Control Using Alternating Magnetic Field Forces (2026)
sources.evidence: Three units on linear air tracks. Frequency selection is an option for interaction management; this is a constrained ground demonstration.

sources.title: Hartwig et al., The SPARC Toroidal Field Model Coil Program
sources.access: Preprint abstract plus existing repository report
sources.evidence: High-current, high-field REBCO prototype precedent. The assumed 100 A/mm2 engineering current density at low field, cryostat, cooling and kilometer deployment remain extrapolations.

sources.title: Bamford et al., Minimagnetospheres above the Lunar Surface and the Formation of Lunar Swirls (2012)
sources.evidence: Observed, theoretical and laboratory electron-scale barriers; ions can be turned electrostatically even when unmagnetized. Ion gyroradius alone cannot reject a small barrier, and vacuum magnetic pressure alone cannot accept one.

sources.title: Fundamentals of the Plasma Sail Concept: MHD and Kinetic Studies (2003)
sources.evidence: MHD size assumptions need kinetic review when the proposed bubble is comparable to or smaller than solar-wind ion scales.

sources.title: Gunell et al., Why an intrinsic magnetic field does not protect a planet against atmospheric escape (2018)
sources.access: Existing protection report and published primary research
sources.evidence: Field topology and escape channels matter; particle deflection is not atmospheric-retention proof.

sources.title: Ambroglini et al., Evaluation of Superconducting Magnet Shield Configurations for Long Duration Manned Space Missions (2016)
sources.access: Existing protection report and published primary research
sources.evidence: Particle transport and secondaries determine dose; BL diagnostics alone provide no dose reduction.

sources.title: NASA Small Spacecraft Technology, Power (2026)
sources.evidence: Modern space PV and Li-ion component benchmarks. Cell specific energy is not pack specific energy; 150/200 Wh/kg pack cases and 400 Wh/kg exploratory case are expressly assumptions.

sources.title: Design Considerations for Lightweight Space Radiators Based on Fabrication and Test Experience with a Carbon-Carbon Composite Prototype Heat Pipe (1998)
sources.evidence: Prototype-derived radiator-element mass, not a complete deployed system. This study uses an explicit 5 kg/m2 system allowance and temperature sensitivity instead of adopting the element value.

sources.title: NIST CODATA 2022 proton mass
sources.evidence: 1.67262192595e-27 kg added as a shared named constant.

sources.title: Measuring the permittivity of fused silica with planar on-wafer structures up to 325 GHz
sources.evidence: Relative permittivity 3.87 and loss tangent below 0.005 across 320 MHz–325 GHz motivate a bare-substrate sensitivity. No complete shield-assembly transmission is inferred.

engineering_scenarios.microwave: 5.8 GHz; 70% electric-to-RF, 85% RF-to-electric, 90% capture, 95% receiver bus; 100 m aperture; 1 kW/m2 peak received beam flux.
engineering_scenarios.laser: 1064 nm; 50% electric-to-optical and 50% optical-to-electric, 90% capture, 95% bus; 1 m transmit aperture; deliberately broadened beam limited to 5 kW/m2 peak flux. Neither efficiency nor MW module scale is demonstrated here.
engineering_scenarios.power_mass: 300 W/kg gross solar-array system, 1000 W/kg conversion/PMAD equipment, 2 kg/m2 receiver, 5 kg/m2 transmit aperture and radiator. Include cooling separately; vary critical estimates in report.
engineering_scenarios.solar_array: 30% conversion, 0.9 absorptivity, both faces at emissivity 0.85, independent Sun tracking and no shadows. An imposed design case requiring new dynamics and visibility tests.
engineering_scenarios.coil: 100 A/mm2 engineering current density, density 6000 kg/m3 and 1 MJ/kg working specific strength inherited from the September protection scenario. Thin square loops for interactions; equivalent-perimeter circular self-inductance and tensile support. 0.1 m equivalent bundle radius, 0.25 m cryostat radius, 5 kg/m cryostat, 0.05 W/m2 cold heat leak, COP 0.005; 300 W/kg refrigerator input equipment. At least one full winding per tile; three-axis actuation is additional equipment.
engineering_scenarios.plasma: Quiet: 5/cm3, 400 km/s, 10 eV electrons, 5 nT IMF. Compressed: 20/cm3, 800 km/s, 20 eV, 15 nT. Severe: 100/cm3, 800 km/s, 30 eV, 30 nT. Scenario envelope, not a forecast. Also retain inherited 2/20/100 nPa pressures.
engineering_scenarios.renewal: 5/20/100 year service-life scenarios, 100 MJ/kg manufacturing energy, 99.9% material recovery sensitivity. No measured lifetime for the proposed installations. Batteries additionally depend on equivalent full cycles.
